sections.markdown:
## C — Tests, permits, skills test and renewal

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Staff ask a few general health questions, and doubt about your physical fitness to drive can hold the application pending a reexamination with more medical information. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
If you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision test, your license will require you to wear them while driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Failing the vision test means an eye-care specialist must complete a vision statement, and limits such as daylight driving only may follow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
For a knowledge test toward an original operator’s, chauffeur’s or commercial license, arrive at least one hour before the office closes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
Knowledge tests come in many languages, and foreign language interpreters may help on every written test except commercial license knowledge tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
A temporary instruction permit (TIP) is valid for 180 days and lets you practice with a licensed adult before the driving skills test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
TIPs go to people never licensed, foreign license holders seeking a Michigan license, and people whose license expired at least four years ago. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
To get a TIP you bring the four proofs, pass the vision test and health standards plus the written knowledge and road sign tests, pay the fee and have your photo taken. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
You must practice on a TIP for at least 30 days before the driving skills test, and an adult driver education course is encouraged. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
After the department receives your skills test results, your license is mailed, and a temporary operator’s permit printed from your MiLogin account lets you drive until it arrives. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A02
Any special licensing conditions or restrictions are printed on the license, and drivers licensed for the first time are on probation for at least three years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A02
The motorcycle TIP lets a new rider practice on public roads under constant supervision of an experienced motorcyclist, and it never replaces the endorsement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle TIP lasts 180 days, and no rider receives more than two of them in a 10-year period. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle TIP requires age 16, a valid Michigan driver’s license, passing the vision and motorcycle knowledge tests, and the fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle TIP rider must stay in constant visual supervision of a licensed motorcycle operator aged at least 18, and may not ride at night or carry passengers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
A driving skills test is required for Level 2, for never-licensed applicants 18 or older, when your last license expired more than four years ago, or for a license from a country other than Canada, Germany or South Korea. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A02
Under-18 skills test applicants need Segment 2 completed, Level 1 held at least six months, and a log of at least 50 supervised hours with 10 at night, kept in The Supervised Driving Guide or the free RoadReady app. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
Under-18 applicants must also have no convictions, civil infractions, suspensions or at-fault crashes in the 90 days right before the skills test and Level 2 application. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A02
Applicants 18 or older must hold a TIP before the skills test, and a 30-day practice period may be required. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A02
Independent businesses approved by the Secretary of State give skills tests, and since the state does not set their fees, ask about pricing before you book. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A02
Hard-of-hearing or non-fluent applicants may use an interpreter in the skills test, who must show photo ID and only relay the examiner’s instructions, but not in commercial license written or skills tests. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A03
The skills test starts with off-street, closed-course maneuvers, and only after passing them do you take the on-road test that earns the driving skills receipt. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A03
The on-road portion includes urban, expressway, rural highway and residential driving, as described in the Driving Skills Test Study Guide. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
A Physician’s Statement of Examination may be requested at application or renewal for any physical or mental condition that may affect safe driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A03
A physician’s statement is also required when the state has reason to believe you had a seizure, blackout, fainting spell or other loss of consciousness within the past six months. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A03
Chauffeur and commercial license holders must have had no blackouts, fainting spells or seizures in the last 12 months. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A03
A physician or physician’s assistant licensed in Michigan or another state completes the statement, describing conditions and medications, and the Driver Assessment Section reviews it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A03
A serious condition reported at renewal leads to a driver reexamination, so start renewing several weeks early, and a restricted license for illness may bring periodic reexams. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A03
New drivers, GDL teens included, stay on probation for at least three years, a monitoring program kept separate from GDL. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A03
To change your name, change it with the Social Security Administration first, wait at least three business days, then bring your license and name-change proof to an office for a new license and fee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A03
Michigan law requires your license address to match your residence and your voter identification card, and address changes are free online, in person or by mail. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A03
An online address change updates your license or ID, your voter registration, and vehicle records linked to your license account. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A04
Vehicles not linked to your license account get the new address only during a vehicle transaction, and failing to report a move can bring suspension or revocation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A04
A license is usually valid four years and expires on your birthday in the year printed on it, except that under-21 licenses expire on the 21st birthday. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A04
The renewal notice goes to the address on record, driving without a valid license is illegal, and renewing after expiration adds a late fee. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A04
A suspended, revoked or denied license cannot be renewed, and renewal can be refused without a valid Social Security number or ineligibility letter and legal presence proof. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A04
When no office visit is required, you may renew by mail, online at Michigan.gov/SOS or at a self-service station. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A04
Every 12 years you must renew in person at an office, where vision is screened and a new photo is taken. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F39 | anchor: A04
Someone who stops driving returns the license to an office and applies for a state ID card instead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-F40 | anchor: A04
Free ID cards go to people who are legally blind, drivers 65 or older who voluntarily give up their license, and drivers who lose driving privileges for a physical or mental disability. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]
